articles.title: Identifiability of Sequential LLM Rewriting Channels
articles.notes: Markov-kernel theory of when an ordered sequence of LLM rewrites is recoverable from the final text law. Observational equivalence, source-relative noncommutativity, a closed-form provenance horizon, and an Assouad bound showing the number of recoverable lineage positions does not grow with depth. Complete draft; pending novelty verification.
articles.abstract: A document produced by one language model may be rewritten by others before anyone sees it, so the observable text is the endpoint of a latent sequence of stochastic transformations. Modelling each rewriting mechanism as a Markov kernel and a lineage as an ordered composition of kernels, we ask when the lineage is identifiable from the law of the final text.

articles.title: Statistical Dynamics of Sequentially Rewritten LLM Text
articles.notes: Dynamical companion to Paper 1: attractors and cycle attractors under repeated rewriting, an autonomy criterion for signature recursions, invariant and quasi-invariant statistics, spectral persistence, and the robustness-versus-identifiability trade-off.
articles.abstract: Repeated rewriting of a document by stochastic text transformations induces a dynamical system on the law of the text, and on any measurable signature of it. That successive paraphrasing by language models produces attractors and cycles is documented empirically; we ask what a contraction hypothesis actually delivers, and which observables survive it.

articles.title: Tracing the Rewrite Chain: Recovering Ordered LLM Provenance from Final Text
articles.notes: Empirical lineage reconstruction: labelled rewrite-chain datasets, ordered-path estimators, benchmark protocol, and provenance-depth curves testing the predictions of Papers 1 and 2. Gated on data and compute access.
articles.abstract: This manuscript is reserved for empirical reconstruction of ordered LLM rewrite histories from final text. It will evaluate whether model-specific statistical traces permit recovery of latent rewrite paths under controlled and realistic transformations.

articles.title: Sequential Watermark Dynamics under Repeated LLM Rewriting
articles.notes: Controlled special case on multi-stage watermark attenuation, interference, collision, and order effects. Deliberately gated on finding a sharper contribution than 'multiple watermarks can coexist or decay'.
articles.abstract: This manuscript is reserved for the explicit-watermark special case of sequential text rewriting. Its intended focus is the evolution, coexistence, interference, and possible order information of multiple statistical watermark signals under repeated rewriting.

articles.title: Uncertainty and Calibration Under Shift, Noise, and Autocorrelation: A Simulation Benchmark
articles.notes: Simulation benchmark for uncertainty in regression, classification, and forecasting under shift, noise, and temporal dependence.
articles.abstract: We present uncertainty-bench, a fully reproducible simulation benchmark for predictive uncertainty under dataset shift, class imbalance with label noise, and temporal dependence. All claims are generated from scripted artifacts and traced to results/aggregated/metrics_summary.csv.

articles.title: Stress-Testing Online Change-Point Detection Under Missingness, Outliers, and Seasonality: A Simulation Study
articles.notes: Main CPD simulation paper.
articles.abstract: Classical online change-point detectors are widely deployed but poorly understood under the data corruption that real-world monitoring systems routinely face: outlier contamination, sensor dropout, and strong seasonality. We present a complete engineering pipeline-seasonal residualization, bounded-influence M-estimation, per-variant threshold calibration, and detection clustering-that makes three sequential detectors (Page-Hinkley, two-sided CUSUM, BOCPD) practical under these conditions, along with a simulation framework for systematic evaluation.

articles.title: Geodesic Non-Local Means for Geometry-Aware Image Denoising
articles.notes: Research codebase for geometry-aware image denoising with reliable baselines, graph-based geodesic denoising methods, reproducible experiments, and publication-ready paper artifacts (figures, tables, and LaTeX alignment).

articles.title: TMLE Missingness Simulation Study
articles.notes: Simulation study comparing MI + Rubin versus missingness-aware orthogonal estimators with bootstrap or BLB inference for causal effects under missing data.
articles.abstract: Orthogonal estimators such as augmented inverse probability weighting (AIPW) and targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE) are widely used to estimate causal effects in observational studies, often with flexible machine learning nuisance fits and cross-fitting. In practice, missing outcomes are commonly handled by complete-case analysis or multiple imputation (MI) followed by Rubin's rules.

articles.title: Curvature-Adaptive k-NN on Nonlinear Manifolds
articles.notes: Research codebase for curvature-adaptive nearest-neighbour classification, including fixed-k, curvature-adaptive, and curvature-weighted k-NN with reproducible synthetic benchmarks, runtime tracking, and paper artifact generation.
articles.abstract: This preprint studies a concrete question in nearest-neighbour learning: when does locally adaptive neighbourhood size produce measurable headroom over strong fixed-(k) and non-curvature baselines, and can that headroom be recovered by a deployable proxy? The repository answers this question through a fully reproducible benchmark stack with three layers: an original local-PCA residual proxy, an oracle local-optimal-(k) diagnostic that measures the attainable adaptive ceiling, and supervised proxy estimators that attempt to approximate that ceiling from training labels alone without query-time leakage.

articles.title: Economic Crises as Redistribution Operators: A Dynamical Systems Model of Wage Decline, Wealth Concentration, and Policy Control
articles.notes: Reproducible research repo with formal dynamical systems model, ETL pipeline for inequality/macro/labour data, simulation code, empirical panel analysis, and policy counterfactuals. Treats crisis outcomes as government choices.
articles.abstract: This article studies a distributional pattern that appears in several modern crises: real wages fall or stagnate while wealth at the top of the distribution rises. The paper formalises this pattern as a controlled dynamical system.

articles.title: Wealth Concentration as a Destructive Attractor: A Conditional Dynamical-Systems Benchmark
articles.notes: Benchmark two-variable dynamical-systems paper proving conditional local collapse stability under explicit institutional and demand-side thresholds, with equilibrium geometry, basin structure, separatrix analysis, and bifurcation results. Model-internal and non-empirical by design.
articles.abstract: Can wealth concentration become a locally self-reinforcing boundary state in a reduced-form political-economy dynamics? This article studies the general two-state class x=x(1-x)F(x,y) and y=yG(x,y), where x is a normalised concentration or effective-power index and y is a normalised demand-support/activity index.

articles.title: From Destructive Attractors to Institutional Resilience: Calibration, Stochastic Escape, and Policy Counterfactuals
articles.notes: Extension paper adding public-data calibration, SMM and ABC identification checks, weak-identification diagnostics, three-variable bargaining dynamics, ABM consistency, stochastic escape, EVT-style rare-event analysis, and policy counterfactuals. Uses the benchmark theorem from Paper 1 without re-proving it.
articles.abstract: This article turns the benchmark destructive-attractor model into a calibrated computational stress test. Using a pooled public-indicator panel, we ask not whether the benchmark theorem is universally true, but whether the proxy-mapped economies in the current sample sit near the model's collapse region, how sharply the relevant margins are informed, and how policy and stochastic perturbations move the system once calibration uncertainty is admitted.

articles.title: From Bargaining Collapse to Institutional Erosion: Higher-Dimensional Destructive Attractor Models
articles.notes: Higher-dimensional theory paper developing the 3D bargaining model and 4D endogenous-institutions model as a hierarchy extending the 2D benchmark. Focuses on forward invariance, equilibria, resilience regions, deterministic simulations, basin slices, and continuation diagnostics.

articles.title: Monte Carlo Cartography of Destructive Attractors: Collapse Probabilities, Resilience Thresholds, and Global Sensitivity
articles.notes: Computational uncertainty paper building a Monte Carlo atlas across the 2D, 3D, and 4D model hierarchy. Covers parameter and initial-condition uncertainty, stochastic shocks, collapse and resilience probability maps, first-passage summaries, and global sensitivity analysis without making empirical-probability claims.

articles.title: Koopman Early-Warning Indicators for Destructive Attractors in Political-Economy Dynamical Systems
articles.notes: Methodological paper applying Koopman operator methods and EDMD to derive slow modes, basin-separating observables, and short-window collapse predictors across the model hierarchy. Emphasizes model-internal diagnostics, spectral comparison, and robustness rather than empirical forecasting.

articles.title: Topological Cartography of Collapse and Resilience: Morse Graphs and Basin Structure in Destructive-Attractor Models
articles.notes: Set-oriented topology paper constructing coarse global state-space summaries through box decompositions, transition graphs, recurrent components, Morse-style graphs, and basin comparisons across 2D, 3D, and 4D models. Claims are explicitly resolution- and flow-time-dependent rather than theorem-level topology statements.

articles.title: Determinants of Municipal House Prices in Portugal: Structure, Space, and the Limits of a Short Panel
articles.notes: Preprint (article/ARTICLE.tex, PDF built, dated July 2026) extending the published municipal-level analysis with auditable open-data ETL, validation, model-ready datasets, panel econometrics, spatial diagnostics and spatial models, RNAL exposure collection, causal scaffolds, granular data architecture, and temporal clustering. Keeps two price-definition families strictly separate and never merges them into one dependent variable: PORDATA transaction values (2011 Census cross-section, 2009-2019 annual panel) and INE median EUR/m2 (2021 cross-section, 2019-2022 annual panel). The repository is explicit that substantive empirical claims depend on official input data, that spatial, clustering, and causal layers have distinct inferential status, and that its own temporal clustering was demoted to a weak exploratory result. Reproduce with scripts/reproduce_paper.sh; provenance in reproducibility_metadata.json, data_manifest.csv, and CITATION.cff.
articles.abstract: We revisit and extend a municipal-level analysis of Portuguese house prices built on a single 2017 cross-section of all 308 municipalities. We first reproduce the published specification exactly (adjusted R^2=0.7121, n=308) on the original study dataset, and then construct a separate continuation from open administrative and statistical sources-INE and PORDATA indicators, the Ministry of Justice transaction-value series, official boundaries, the short-term-rental register and Census variables-documenting explicitly where the original variables can and cannot be reconstructed faithfully.

articles.title: From Chaos to Crisis: Using Dynamical-Systems Extreme Value Theory in Econometrics
articles.notes: Applies extreme value theory from dynamical systems (Milhazes Freitas framework) to econometric analysis of rare events, crises, and tail dependence. Includes simulation utilities for chaotic maps, rare-event diagnostics (exceedances, extremal index, return/hitting times), multivariate stress analysis, and reproduction package with YAML-based experiment orchestration. Designed for both Medium article and future formal paper.
articles.abstract: Standard stress diagnostics in applied econometrics usually measure magnitude, tail loss, or event frequency, but not the temporal organization of extreme episodes. That omission matters whenever interpretation depends on whether extremes arrive as isolated shocks or as clustered stress.

articles.title: From Wages to Wealth: A Dynamical Model and Research Design for Rent Extraction, Property Ownership, and Class Reproduction
articles.notes: Develops a political-economy model of wealth concentration centered on the conversion of wages into asset ownership, with housing as the main transmission channel. Includes a deterministic dynamic model with explicit ownership-transition timing and affordability constraints, Portugal-oriented calibration scenarios, fixed-effects panel utilities, household ownership-transition modeling, dashboards, notebooks, and a reproducible simulation pipeline. The current empirical layer is implemented in code but still relies on synthetic sample panel data and provisional calibration anchors, so the repo is best understood as a theory-plus-research-design package for a working paper and future formal article.
articles.abstract: Inequality is not exhausted by differences in labour income: it also depends on whether households can convert current income into appreciating assets before housing costs, debt service, and asset-price inflation absorb their residual surplus. This paper develops a deterministic two-type accumulation model-renters versus owners-in which a moving down-payment threshold and a debt-service-to-income cap govern who crosses into ownership, and proves how rent burden, house-price growth, and policy instruments shape that transition.

articles.title: The European Economy as a Set of Choices: A Reusable Diagnostic Framework for Convergence, Wages, Investment, and Fiscal Policy
articles.notes: Policy-facing analytical framework for diagnosing the European economy through economic choices rather than headline GDP. Implements a synthetic EU macro-panel generator, growth and beta/sigma convergence analysis, wage-productivity gap and labour/profit-share diagnostics, public and private investment indicators, fiscal-stance classification, inflation and real-wage pressure measures, inequality indicators, country scorecards, and an automated Portugal-vs-EU policy brief, exposed through a Typer CLI, notebooks, and tests. The framework currently runs offline on synthetic panels with an explicit extension path to Eurostat, AMECO, and ECB data, so it is best understood as a reusable diagnostic toolkit awaiting connection to official sources.

articles.title: Has Supply-Side Liberalisation Been Tested? Event Studies, Synthetic Control, and Panel Evidence on Its Promised Gains
articles.notes: Reproducible empirical project that treats the supply-side liberalisation package (lower income and corporate taxes, privatisation, labour-market flexibility, a smaller public sector) as a falsifiable claim and tests whether it historically delivered higher productivity, real wages, GDP per capita, and lower poverty. Combines event studies around policy episodes (Portugal 2011-2015, Kansas 2012-2017, UK post-1979, US post-1981, Eastern European flat-tax reforms), a synthetic-control design for Portugal, and OECD/EU panel models, alongside an indicator contract, source registry, methodology notes, notebook templates, a Django dashboard scaffold, and tests. The analytical scaffolding, reusable functions, and agent prompts are in place, but the data providers are not yet fully connected, so the empirical conclusions remain to be produced under the repository's explicit robustness and failure-criteria rules.

articles.title: Could Portugal Build a Sovereign Fund from Social Security Surpluses? A Monte Carlo Stress-Testing Framework
articles.notes: Transparent Monte Carlo stress-testing framework (explicitly not a forecast) for whether Portugal could build a sovereign or strategic fund via the indirect route of Social Security surpluses, FEFSS transfers, and financial-asset purchases. Anchored on editable 2025 fiscal and FEFSS baselines, it simulates public-debt trajectories, FEFSS pension-coverage ratios, sovereign-fund asset growth, and downside risk across six policy scenarios spanning conservative reinforcement, debt-reduction-first, higher-equity mandates, indirect and aggressive strategic funds, and a post-2035 demographic-stress case. A second engine isolates the specific risk of buying Portuguese equities with pension surpluses, using transparent proxy returns by default and optional downloaded market data. The model deliberately separates fiscal balance, financial allocation, and mandate, and is designed to be falsifiable and improvable with better demographic and return calibration.

articles.title: From Employer Wages to State Transfers: A Ten-Paper Programme on Poverty, the Low-Wage Subsidy State, and Asset Power in the US and UK Since 1950
articles.notes: Agent-first scaffold for a sequenced ten-paper empirical research programme sharing one data pipeline, modelling framework, set of definitions, and reproducibility contract. It tests the working hypothesis that since the Reagan and Thatcher periods poverty reduction shifted away from employer responsibility and wage growth toward state correction through taxes and transfers, while the upper tail increasingly captured income via assets, business ownership, and capital gains taxed differently from wages - that is, that public budgets increasingly subsidised low wages as asset owners captured a growing share of income and wealth. The papers span the historical poverty record, lagged policy effects, market versus state-corrected poverty, the low-wage subsidy state, the incidence of poverty reduction, asset income and top wealth, labour power, housing, synthetic counterfactuals, and a final synthesis. The specification, data contracts, and per-paper prompts are complete; the empirical work is deliberately left minimal for a coding agent to implement, and the repo is explicit that the hypothesis must be tested rather than assumed and that synthetic data must not be used as evidence.

articles.title: North–South Fire-Season Onset in Mainland Portugal: A Reproducible Data-Engineering and Statistics Pipeline
articles.notes: Tests whether rural fire onset is earlier at higher latitude, keeping ignition, burned-area, and fire-weather onset separate. Multi-source ingestion (ICNF, NASA FIRMS, EFFIS, ERA5/CEMS, GISCO, CORINE/DGT COS, DEM, OSM, INE) via a provenance-tracked download manager into PostGIS. Pure-Python statistics (OLS+robust SE, sign test, permutation, discrete-time hazard, Cox PH, Weibull AFT, random-intercept mixed, quantile, robustness). All 29 prompts implemented; ruff+mypy clean; 197 unit tests; offline path (features onset -> stats run -> viz build) reproducible. Remaining: live credentialed downloads (FIRMS/CDS), live PostGIS loader run, real GeoTIFF raster reads. Article is a scaffold, not yet written.

articles.title: Can Portugal Produce a Parish-Level Map of Rent per Square Metre? A Coverage and Concordance Audit of Official INE Rent Data
articles.notes: Reproducible pipeline auditing whether a national parish-level (freguesia) rent-per-m2 map can be built from observed official INE data alone, with explicit coverage reporting, CAOP 2025 concordance, and strict separation of official / asking-price / inferred / modelled layers.

articles.title: Locating Where Extreme-Score Detectors Fail: A Layered Evaluation for Predictive Maintenance on Public Industrial Data
articles.notes: Reproducible layered evaluation that separates an extreme-score detector into score, threshold, extreme clusters, alarm episodes and matched events, so failure can be located per method rather than per dataset. Applied to two independent held-out compressor failures (MetroPT, MetroPT2) across nineteen methods under one shared alarm policy, with a warning-window rank separation and a circular-shift null that test whether a match carries information, genuine cross-dataset target-region transfer, detection-conditioned matched controls, and a high-replication extremal-index Monte Carlo. Under major revision after peer review; archived at Zenodo (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21803768), results correspond to release v0.3.2.
articles.abstract: Does a dynamical-EVT workflow turn clustered extreme scores into useful maintenance alarms on public industrial monitoring data? On this evidence, no.

articles.title: Portugal's Public-Debt Interest Burden: Measurement and Debt Dynamics under ESA 2010
articles.notes: Reproducible annual dataset and paper on general-government interest payable (Eurostat D41PAY) in euros and as a share of nominal GDP, with an optional AMECO pre-1995 extension kept separate and observed/forecast observations labelled. Decomposes the decline in the burden into effective rate, debt ratio, nominal growth, and inflation, and compares Portugal against the euro-area universe under harmonised definitions. Ships validation and reproducibility JSON, generated LaTeX tables, and a committed PDF built from paper/portugal_public_debt_interest_report.tex.

articles.title: The Repricing Kernel: How Fast Do Market Rates Pass Through to Portugal's Effective Debt Cost?
articles.notes: Second paper in the same repository, relaxing the burden paper's constant-hazard repricing assumption. Imports rather than duplicates the shared measurement layer, with a regression test asserting the burden paper's artefacts stay byte-identical. Every manuscript number is a generated macro; a gate fails the build if a literal is hand-typed. Null results are reported alongside positive ones in reports/repricing/findings.md.
articles.abstract: Weighted average maturity is a natural first statistic for judging how quickly a rate shock reaches a sovereign interest bill. It is also easy to overuse.

articles.title: Short-Term Interest Rate Innovations Across Monetary Regimes
articles.notes: Evidence-gated scaffold for replicating and extending Maio and Santa-Clara on short-rate innovations and equity anomalies, asking whether the innovation prices anomalies as a stable hedging state variable or as a mix of policy shocks, central-bank information, macro news, and regime-dependent transmission. Two deliberately separate tracks: strict replication and documented reconstruction, which never labels substitutes as reproduced. Config, typed pipeline interfaces, validation, and tests are in place; data acquisition is intentionally disabled until licences and variable definitions are recorded in research/data_access_matrix.csv. Release gate reports 0 critical and 1 major issue: code release permitted, empirical-results release blocked.

articles.title: Dimensional Asymptotics of Euler-Based Simulated Likelihood for Multidimensional Diffusions
articles.notes: Shows the endpoint/Pedersen simulated-likelihood estimator is a shrinking-bandwidth kernel estimator of bandwidth sqrt(h), giving effective simulation size S / M^(K/2) rather than S. Derives exact finite-M moments, the local moment law, corrected density-level normalisation, and an MSE minimised at M ~ S^(2/(K+4)), then gives a sharp counterexample refuting the joint transition-density consistency and CLT lemmas of Brandt and Santa-Clara (2002) for K > 2. Explicitly does not claim the argmax estimator is inconsistent - proves the opposite in a Gaussian location model on the same designs - and does not claim the published empirical estimates are wrong; the open question is the rate. A companion note handles the exchange-rate application (Feller ratios, incompleteness, invertibility, identification), with several deliberately negative results. Both manuscripts compile with all figures and tables generated from the code; 39 DOIs Crossref-verified.
articles.abstract: A widely used simulation method for likelihood inference in discretely observed diffusions approximates each transition density by simulating an Euler scheme to one step before the observed endpoint and averaging the final Gaussian density. We show that this endpoint estimator is a shrinking-bandwidth kernel estimator whose effective simulation size is S/M^K/2, not S, where K is the state dimension, M the number of Euler substeps and S the number of simulations.

articles.title: Persistent Continuous Price-Level Ordering in Portuguese Municipal Housing Across Two Price Constructs
articles.notes: Standalone longitudinal unsupervised paper (not a revision of the earlier municipal house-price determinants work) analysing PORDATA average transaction value 2009-2019 and INE median price per m2 2019-2025 as two separate constructs that are never spliced. Headline estimand is a persistent continuous price-level ordering; two-group tiers are reported only as uncertain, lossy coarsenings, not market types. Separates level, shape, level-plus-shape, and growth representations, with B>=500 bootstrap stability, candidate HMM state formulations, spatial-graph and fold-refit external INE validation, and uncertainty-aware structural profiling. Reports negative results when a structure fails the diagnostic rules rather than forcing a partition. Reviewer-facing run registry records analysis commit, config hash, seed, and data manifest hash. Under major revision.
articles.abstract: We ask which summary of transaction data describes a municipal housing market, and what is lost when a continuous price signal is forced into discrete groups. Using two differently defined Portuguese price constructs that we never splice-an average transaction value from PORDATA (2009-2019) and a median price per square metre from Statistics Portugal (2019-2025)-we find that variation on both is overwhelmingly variation in persistent level.

articles.title: Colonial versus European Linkages in Portuguese Growth, 1960-1973
articles.notes: Data-engineering and analytical code only - the repository deliberately contains no paper, argument, or narrative conclusion until the pipeline, territorial definitions, classifications, and cross-checks are stable. Builds evidence on the shift of Portuguese export destinations across colonial, EFTA, EEC, and other markets, product-group dependence on colonial markets, and openness/trade/GDP evolution, cross-checking UN Comtrade, BPstat, World Bank, CEPII TRADHIST, INE, OECD, and EFTA aggregates. Three-layer raw/interim/processed reproducibility policy with SHA-256 sidecars and manifests; a committed deterministic World Bank bootstrap snapshot makes validation run offline. Explicitly refuses to treat gross exports as GDP or to estimate a net return from colonialism without fiscal, financial, military, and opportunity-cost data. Synthetic records exist only under tests/fixtures.

articles.title: Extending the Municipal Housing-Price Model to Multiple Years
articles.notes: ICCSA/LNCS-formatted extension of the municipal housing-price model from a single cross-section to multiple years, alongside a Portuguese abstract (resumo.tex) and the conference presentation deck (housing_prices_portugal_conference_presentation.tex). Built on the llncs document class. Sits between the published municipal-level analysis and the later panel and trajectory work in housing_future_work_etl and portugal-housing-trajectories.

articles.title: Dynamics of the Real Estate Market: Determining Factors in the Value of Housing in Portugal
articles.notes: Multiple linear regression on PORDATA data for all 308 Portuguese municipalities, identifying the factors driving municipal housing transaction values: location, population density, local purchasing power, family size, unemployment, environmental quality, ageing, education, marital status, owner-occupier ratio, and available housing stock. Finds most factors significant except population density and environmental quality. Framed as decision support for buyers and investors and for municipal-to-national housing policy. NOTE: this 2023 manuscript closely matches the scope of the published ICCSA 2026 paper and may be its pre-publication draft rather than a live article - confirm before working it.
articles.abstract: This study provides decision-making support in the Portuguese housing sector, serving both individual and political stakeholders. For individuals - buyers and investors alike - it offers insights for informed purchasing and investment decisions.

articles.title: When Does Wealth Concentration Become Financial Fragility? An Agent-Based Simulation Laboratory
articles.notes: Agent-based model of heterogeneous agents differing in wealth, income, debt, and marginal propensity to consume. When capital returns rise with existing wealth, income and wealth concentrate among high-saving agents, aggregate consumption weakens, lower- and middle-wealth agents borrow to defend a consumption floor, and private debt accumulates until default or output-collapse thresholds are crossed. Monte Carlo experiments characterise how crisis probability, timing, and severity vary with the concentration-strength parameter, and a mechanism-specific falsification suite shows crises weaken or disappear when individual channels are removed. Optional firm, banking, and asset-collateral sectors. The stated contribution is mechanism integration, scenario grids, and falsification - explicitly demonstrating causal sufficiency in silico, uncalibrated, and explicitly not empirical causal proof.
articles.abstract: This paper studies the conditions under which wealth concentration turns into financial fragility. We develop an agent-based simulation in which heterogeneous agents differ in wealth, income, debt, and marginal propensity to consume.

articles.title: Heat-Burst-Like Extremes as Rare Transitions in a Reduced Downdraft System
articles.notes: Hybrid framework coupling a reduced-order dynamical model of precipitation-driven downdrafts to peaks-over-threshold Extreme Value Theory, for thunderstorm heat bursts - rare, short-lived events hard to study from station records alone. The dynamical part models a two-layer hydrostatic background with a stable nocturnal near-surface layer beneath a deep near-dry-adiabatic residual layer, with cloud-base geometry, evaporation, condensate-loaded negative buoyancy, rain-water exhaustion, entrainment, drag, and dry adiabatic compressional warming. The statistical part estimates the tail of a composite severity index from temperature jump, dew-point drop, and downdraft speed. Synthetic experiments reproduce heat-burst-like warming as a tail population, with the strongest baseline events exceeding ten degrees. Explicitly a controlled mechanism study, not an operational forecasting system or a replacement for convection-resolving NWP. Manuscript is arXiv-oriented (paper/README_ARXIV.md).
articles.abstract: Thunderstorm heat bursts are localized events characterized by abrupt surface warming, sharp drying, and gusty winds. They are rare, short-lived, and difficult to study from station records alone.

articles.title: How Fast Would Carbon Capture Have to Grow? A Transparent, Reproducible Feasibility-Gap Assessment of Mid-Century CCS Deployment
articles.notes: Tests whether the multi-gigatonne mid-century CCS assumed by Paris-consistent mitigation pathways is consistent with the observed starting point - current operating capacity plus the announced project pipeline - using a deliberately transparent reproducible framework rather than an integrated assessment model. Reaching a representative 6 GtCO2/yr subsurface-storage benchmark by 2050 from about 50 MtCO2/yr operating in early 2025 requires a sustained CAGR of roughly 21 percent. Deliberately narrow: it does not claim CCS is impossible, only that the scale, speed, infrastructure, land, reservoir, and cost requirements of CCS-heavy pathways are far beyond current deployment. Has revision notes and both Markdown and LaTeX manuscripts.
articles.abstract: Many integrated mitigation pathways consistent with the Paris Agreement assume that carbon capture and storage (CCS) reaches multiple gigatonnes of CO₂ per year by mid-century. We test whether that assumption is consistent with the observed starting point — current operating capacity and the announced project pipeline — using a deliberately transparent, fully reproducible framework rather than a complex integrated assessment model.

articles.title: The heteroTests Package: A Unified Toolkit for Heteroscedasticity Diagnostics
articles.notes: R Journal submission (RJwrapper/RJtemplate layout, compiled PDF present) for an R package implementing a broad collection of heteroscedasticity diagnostics for linear models - White, Breusch-Pagan, Goldfeld-Quandt and others - plus helpers to visualise and mitigate heteroscedasticity. Every test returns a base-R htest object and follows a common perform*Test(model, data, ...) convention so results print, subset, and compose like stats::bptest() and drop into automated pipelines. Repo carries fixes.md and fixes_1.md revision notes.
articles.abstract: Heteroscedasticity tests are fragmented across over a dozen R packages, forcing users to juggle differing function names, arguments, and outputs. heteroTests resolves this by wrapping 25+ popular diagnostics—spanning auxiliary‐regression, group‐comparison, rank‐based, nonconstant‐variance, and ARCH‐type methods—into a single, consistent API. Each perform*Test() returns a standardized S3 htest object enriched with metadata (residual type, trimming, lags, grouping), enabling batch execution and automated reporting via runHeteroTests().

articles.title: High-Order Navier-Stokes Solvers for Transitional and Turbulent Flows
articles.notes: Unified computational framework for the 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations combining a Newton-Raphson finite-difference scheme with multigrid pressure correction and a Fourier pseudospectral solver with hyperviscosity, stochastic large-scale forcing, and adaptive time stepping. Covers formulation, discretisation, and algorithmic enhancements, with validation showing spectral accuracy on canonical benchmarks and scaling studies confirming strong parallel efficiency. Both solvers share a configuration system, automated testing, and publication-ready assets (manuscript, figures, slides).
articles.abstract: We present a unified computational framework for the two-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations that combines a Newton-Raphson finite difference scheme with a Fourier spectral solver. The accompanying open-source implementation emphasises reproducibility, modularity, and high performance across transitional and turbulent regimes.

articles.title: Restricted Mean Survival Time Versus Classical Tests: A Comprehensive Simulation-Based Comparison of Statistical Power
articles.notes: Simulation framework comparing RMST against the logrank test, Peto-Peto Wilcoxon, and Cox PH across 24 survival scenarios including proportional hazards, early benefit, delayed benefit, crossing hazards, and diminishing effects, with 5,000 replications per scenario and 200-1,000 participants per arm. Evaluates type I error control, power, and sensitivity to the truncation horizon. Shipped as an installable R package with vignettes and a YAML-driven CLI for batch runs. INCOMPLETE: the manuscript's Results section is still a placeholder ('to be completed') covering type I error rates, power comparisons, truncation-time guidance, and sample-size recommendations.
articles.abstract: Background: Traditional survival analysis methods, including the Cox proportional hazards model and logrank test, assume proportional hazards (PH) and may lose power or interpretability when this assumption is violated. The restricted mean survival time (RMST) offers a robust alternative that quantifies treatment benefit as the difference in mean survival time up to a prespecified horizon.

articles.title: Comparing Agent-Based and ODE SEIR Models Under Non-Pharmaceutical Interventions
articles.notes: Framework simulating epidemic dynamics with both an agent-based SEIR model - individuals as particles moving in a 2D domain with distance-based infection - and compartmental SEIR models at regional and metapopulation scale with a mobility matrix, used to compare non-pharmaceutical interventions such as lockdown, mobility reduction, and targeted protection of elderly subpopulations. Code, CLI, tests, and an ABM-vs-ODE notebook are in place; the repository describes paper/main.tex as a LaTeX skeleton for writing up results, so the manuscript itself is not yet written.
articles.abstract: We present a simple yet flexible framework for simulating epidemic dynamics using both an agent-based SEIR model and compartmental SEIR models at regional and metapopulation scales. The agent-based model represents individuals as particles moving in a two-dimensional domain, with infection occurring through distance-based contacts.

articles.title: Passive Proximity Inference in Smart Homes Using RSSI Signals and Temporal Context: A Privacy-Conscious, Data-Centric Framework
articles.notes: Infers user proximity in smart homes from passive RSSI signals and annotated behavioural intervals, for continuous unobtrusive monitoring that improves the temporal resolution of presence detection without requiring explicit sensor activations. Combines a preprocessing pipeline turning semi-structured logs into interpretable time series, integration of annotated sleep and timeout intervals, and transparent rule-based proximity labelling. Positioned against prior work needing dense sensor deployments or complex signal processing: lightweight, explainable, and deployable under ethical and privacy constraints. Two manuscript versions tracked (article.tex, article_version_2.tex).
articles.abstract: This study proposes a data-centric methodology for inferring user proximity to IoT sensors in smart home environments, even in the absence of direct sensor activations. Leveraging time-series RSSI (Received Signal Strength Indicator) data, sleep state intervals, and contextual device metadata, we construct a pipeline that integrates heterogeneous data sources to enable behavioral inference.

articles.title: Synthetic Household Electricity Load Generation: A Model Ladder Approach
articles.notes: Synthload generates realistic synthetic household electricity consumption from Spanish GoiEner smart-meter data using a ladder of hierarchical and dynamic linear models capturing time-of-week effects, temperature sensitivity via heating and cooling degree hours, AR(1) or time-varying-coefficient temporal autocorrelation, and household heterogeneity. The package and pipeline are complete, and the manuscript is written: paper/main.tex is a thin wrapper that inputs six substantive section files (introduction, data and methods, dynamic model, factor model, results and validation, conclusion) totalling roughly 54 KB, with a compiled paper/main.pdf.

articles.title: ssspx: Production-Grade Single-Source Shortest Paths in Python (JOSS)
articles.notes: JOSS-format software paper for ssspx, a typed and tested deterministic single-source shortest-paths solver for directed graphs with non-negative weights, following a BMSSP-style divide-and-conquer design (levels, FindPivots, bounded base case) with a switchable frontier, optional constant-outdegree transform, CLI, exports, and a benchmark harness. The software paper is original; the algorithm it implements is from Duan, Mao, Mao, Shu & Yin, 'Breaking the Sorting Barrier for Directed Single-Source Shortest Paths' (arXiv:2504.17033).

articles.title: cfad: A Characteristic Function Anomaly Detector for Financial Time Series (JOSS)
articles.notes: JOSS-format software paper for a Python package detecting structural breaks in financial return series via contour integrals of the empirical characteristic function. Rather than tracking only first and second moments, it monitors changes in the analytic structure of the data-generating law in the complex frequency domain: under diffusive Gaussian dynamics the characteristic function is entire, so a closed contour integral vanishes by Cauchy's theorem, while heavy-tailed and jump processes introduce branch cuts and poles that make the score rise. Combines Cython-accelerated rolling ECF estimation, contour-residue scoring, and sequential CUSUM alarming in one API, plus parametric CF models (Gaussian, NIG, CGMY, Levy-stable) for structural interpretation. Aimed at computational scientists rather than only quantitative finance.

articles.title: loss-functions-gof: A Unified Python Framework for Loss Functions and Goodness-of-Fit Measures (JOSS)
articles.notes: JOSS-format software paper for a Python library providing a unified, extensible framework for loss functions, metrics, and statistical tests, aiming to bridge classical statistical methods and modern deep-learning approaches for model evaluation, optimisation, and analysis. Ships supplementary materials alongside the paper draft.

articles.title: ewma-ad: Robust EWMA Detectors for Streaming Anomaly Detection (JOSS)
articles.notes: JOSS-format software paper for a lightweight implementation of robust exponentially weighted moving average detectors for streaming anomaly detection over smart-home event and value streams, with adaptive sigma updates, an optional outlier-exclusion gate, per-user baselines, seasonality baselines (hour-of-day and hour-of-week), online conformal prediction intervals, and optional Numba JIT acceleration. Exposes a CLI and an AWS Lambda handler for serverless deployment; metrics include precision/recall@k, time-to-detect, hourly false-alarm rate, and interval coverage (PICP).

articles.title: When Political Systems Negate Their Own Values
articles.notes: Research protocol and novelty-audit stage for a formal and comparative theory of political systems that can generate trajectories negating their own legitimating values.

articles.title: Adaptive Tail-Index Threshold Selection: Calibration, Discrimination, and Excess Risk
articles.notes: Separates whether an adaptive rule detects threshold instability from whether acting on that detection improves risk. A hard-prefix compatibility selector for an orthogonalized Hill estimator is calibrated under the exact Pareto null, its discrimination against second-order alternatives measured, and its squared error compared against the no-selection full-grid aggregate with paired differences. It discriminates and does not reduce risk. The manuscript source is not in version control yet -- heavytails gitignores /research/ -- so paper_path is empty; the supporting experiments at n = 10,000 and n = 50,000 are in the repository.
articles.abstract: Adaptive threshold selection is often motivated by the instability of tail-index estimators across the upper order statistics used for estimation. This paper separates two questions that are sometimes conflated: whether a rule detects threshold instability, and whether acting on that detection improves estimation risk. Using a hard-prefix compatibility selector for an orthogonalized Hill-type estimator as a worked case, we calibrate the selector under the exact Pareto null, inspect discrimination against second-order alternatives, and then compare it with the no-selection full-grid aggregate using paired squared-error differences. The selector is most discriminating in the slow Burr rho = -1/4 alternative, yet even there it does not reduce risk in the current experiments. For a fixed candidate vector under exact Pareto sampling, we show that restricting a minimum-variance unbiased full-grid aggregate cannot reduce squared-error risk. This provides the risk benchmark tested directly by the fixed-candidate experiment reported here. Under second-order alternatives, threshold selection is beneficial only when the squared-bias reduction exceeds the variance penalty. The results therefore motivate excess risk, rather than threshold recovery or stability detection alone, as the primary criterion for evaluating adaptive tail-index procedures.
